_source.title: Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions and Condition Statement of Federal Reserve Banks (H.4.1)
_source.issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
_source._licence: A work of the United States federal government. Not subject to copyright in the US; freely redistributable.

_construction: H41_mixed.pdf is the released PDF with pages 6-11 replaced by 200 dpi greyscale JPEG images of themselves, so those pages carry NO text layer. Pages 1-5 are untouched. Nothing else is altered: no content is added, removed or reordered, and every figure in the gold is the Federal Reserve's own. This is disclosed rather than hidden — it is the instrument the task needs, because a parser that cannot reach an image-only page scores zero on it rather than merely misreading it.
_why_this_design: Earlier versions of this task measured whether parsers preserve row/column association in digital tables. Measured across three document families, they largely do: four parsers scored 17-20/20 on an EPD, and agreed on five of six cells of this same H.4.1 table. Disorder is recoverable — a capable model reconstructs the answer from a garbled row. Absence is not. Splitting the document into a text half and an image-only half makes the difference binary per case instead of marginal.
_gold_provenance: Every figure was read by eye off the page rendered at 2.4x, never from a parser's extraction. Each case records the _page it came from and whether that page is text or image (_layer).

cases.label: Reconstruct a year-ago share from the change column
cases.question: In table 1A, "Memorandum Items", marketable U.S. Treasury securities are one component of the securities held in custody for foreign official and international accounts. Using the week-ended figures and the change from a year earlier, what share of that custody total did marketable Treasuries represent a year ago?
cases._why: The year-ago level is not printed anywhere. It has to be rebuilt by undoing the change column on both the component and the total, then divided. A solution that reads the current share off the page answers 90.44% and is wrong.

cases.label: Identify the dominant driver of the weekly change
cases.question: Reserve balances at Federal Reserve Banks fell over the week ended Jul 29, 2026. Looking at table 1, "Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions", which single factor absorbing reserve funds moved the most over that week, and by how much?
cases.answer: The U.S. Treasury, General Account, up 81,153
cases._why: Nothing names the row. The whole change-from-last-week column has to be scanned and the largest absolute move picked out, then attributed to its label.

cases.label: Average versus point-in-time on the same row
cases.question: table 1A, "Memorandum Items" reports securities lent to dealers twice: as an average of daily figures for the week and as a Wednesday level. Which is larger, and by how much?
cases._why: Two figures on one row under different column groups. A solution that does not distinguish the average from the Wednesday level cannot form the difference.

cases.label: Complement of a share
cases.question: What proportion of the securities held in custody for foreign official and international accounts is made up of something other than marketable U.S. Treasury securities?
cases._why: Requires recognising that the custody total has three components and that the question asks for the two that are not named.

cases.label: Attribute a yearly decline to a sub-line
cases.question: Reverse repurchase agreements in table 1, "Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions" fell over the year. What share of that decline came from the "Others" sub-line rather than from foreign official and international accounts?
cases._why: Both figures sit in the change-from-a-year-ago column, one on the parent row and one on an indented sub-line. The ratio is of two negative changes.

cases.label: Percentage growth off a reconstructed base
cases.question: By what percentage did the U.S. Treasury General Account grow over the year, measured on the week-ended figures in table 1, "Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions"?
cases._why: The base is not printed: it is the current level minus the year change. Dividing the change by the current level instead gives 59.3%, which is the trap.

cases.label: Composition of pledged collateral
cases.question: In table 7, "Collateral Held against Federal Reserve Notes", what share of the Federal Reserve notes to be collateralized is covered by pledged securities rather than by the gold and SDR certificate accounts?
cases._why: Requires reading which of the four collateral lines are certificates and which are securities, then relating to the amount to be collateralized rather than to the collateral total.

cases.label: Headroom, not a printed figure
cases.question: How much more collateral could the Federal Reserve pledge against its notes without acquiring any additional securities?
cases._why: The question names no line. Answering it means understanding that 'eligible to be pledged' in the memo is the ceiling and 'pledged' in the collateral block is the current draw.

cases.label: Concentration across districts
cases.question: In table 6, "Statement of Condition of Each Federal Reserve Bank", which Federal Reserve District holds the largest share of the system total for Deposits, and what share is that?
cases._why: Thirteen columns have to be compared before the ratio can be formed.

cases.label: Share excluded from a requirement
cases.question: What proportion of Federal Reserve notes outstanding is not subject to collateralization?
cases._why: Two adjacent lines, but the denominator is the outstanding figure rather than the to-be-collateralized figure below it.

cases.label: Find the exception in a row
cases.question: In table 6, "Statement of Condition of Each Federal Reserve Bank", earnings remittances due to the U.S. Treasury are negative for most Federal Reserve Districts. Which district shows the largest positive figure, and what is it?
cases._why: Three of the thirteen columns are positive. The row has to be read across, signs kept, and the largest positive picked — not the largest by magnitude, which is negative.

cases.label: An anomalous concentration
cases.question: In table 6, "Statement of Condition of Each Federal Reserve Bank", one district accounts for most of the system total on the indented "Other" line under Deposits. Which district, and what share does it hold?
cases._why: Chicago's figure is four orders of magnitude above its neighbours on that line, so the row must be read across before the share can be computed.

cases.label: Follow the document's own cross-reference
cases.question: The securities figures in table 7, "Collateral Held against Federal Reserve Notes" carry a footnote saying they include securities lent to dealers under the overnight securities lending facility, and pointing to another table for that amount. Find it, and express it as a share of the total U.S. Treasury, agency debt, and mortgage-backed securities reported in that memo.
cases._why: The document itself directs the reader from one table to another, and the two tables sit on opposite sides of the text/image split. The Wednesday column must be chosen in table 1A to match table 7's dating.

cases.label: Two similar-sounding measures
cases.question: Currency in circulation and Federal Reserve notes outstanding are different measures reported in different tables. On Wednesday Jul 29, 2026, by how much do they differ?
cases._why: Neither table names the other. The solution has to know these are distinct quantities and locate each, one on a digital page and one on an image page.

cases.label: Locate a system total inside a district table
cases.question: table 1, "Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions" reports the U.S. Treasury General Account on Wednesday. Looking at table 6, "Statement of Condition of Each Federal Reserve Bank", which single district carries essentially all of it, and what figure does that district show?
cases._why: The system figure is on a digital page and the district breakdown is on an image page; the two agree exactly, which is the check.

cases.label: Composition on one side, total on the other
cases.question: On Wednesday, what share of the system total for reverse repurchase agreements is held for foreign official and international accounts?
cases._why: The split into foreign official and others appears only in table 1 on a digital page; the system total is confirmed in table 6 on an image page. Relabelled from 'both' to 'text': the split into foreign official and others and the system total both sit in table 1, so table 6 adds nothing. A text-only pipeline answered it correctly, which is what exposed the mislabelling.

cases.label: Apply a footnote across the split
cases.question: table 7, "Collateral Held against Federal Reserve Notes" reports securities pledged against Federal Reserve notes, and its footnote says that figure includes securities lent to dealers. If those lent securities were excluded, what would the pledged figure be?
cases._why: Requires reading the footnote on an image page, following it to a digital page for the amount, and subtracting.

cases.label: Reconstruct a district's year-ago share
cases.question: Table 6, "Statement of Condition of Each Federal Reserve Bank", splits depository institution deposits across the twelve Districts. Chicago and Richmond both hold substantial balances. Which of the two holds more, and what is the ratio of the larger to the smaller?
cases._why: Replaced the original question, which asked which District holds foreign official deposits. The closed-book probe answered that correctly with no document — that the New York Fed keeps the foreign official accounts is textbook, not something the release tells you. Chicago against Richmond is not: their relative size on this particular line has to be read. The name requirement was dropped because the question has to name both candidates; the ratio carries the case, and reversing it gives 0.363.

cases.label: Reconcile two different deposit totals
cases.question: Table 1, "Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions", reports deposits held at Federal Reserve Banks other than reserve balances. Table 6, "Statement of Condition of Each Federal Reserve Bank", reports the system total for deposits on the same date. What proportion of that total does table 1’s figure represent?
cases._why: Needs one figure from each half and neither table states the other's. The earlier version asked what the smaller figure leaves out; a text-only pipeline answered it, because table 1 reports reserve balances itself and its 2,944,541 fell inside the tolerance around table 6's 2,944,544.

cases.label: Two conventions for the same instrument
cases.question: table 1, "Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions" reports reverse repurchase agreements on Wednesday, while table 7, "Collateral Held against Federal Reserve Notes" deducts an amount for securities under reverse repurchase agreements. The two figures differ. By how much, and why?
cases.answer: 51,203 — table 1 reports cash value, table 7 face value (388,254 less 337,051)
cases._why: The reason is in the footnotes, one on each side of the split: table 1 note 12 says cash value, table 7's memo line says face value. The two keyword requirements were loosened from 'face value'/'cash value' to the bare words: a correct answer writes it as 'at face' or 'a face measure' as readily as in full, and the stricter form rejected both. Giving the figure with no reason still fails, which is what the requirement is for.

_design: Questions are the kind an analyst actually asks of this release: they name no cell, often no table, and answering them means working out which figures matter and what to do with them. Six need only the digital pages, six only the image pages, and eight need both — those eight cannot be answered at all by a pipeline that reads one half.
